---
title: "Barbara's Portfolio"
---

This website hosts my [portfolio](https://datascience4psych.github.io/DataScience4Psych/guidance.html#portfolio) that I developed as part of [Data Science for Psychologists](https://datascience4psych.github.io/DataScience4Psych/). You can find the links to individual portfolio pieces in the header. Each piece has a description of the goal, the product (computer program, hand graph, computer graph, etc.), the data, and some interpretation. 

The portfolio is organised into three connected mini-projects, all grounded in real eye-movement data analysis. Each piece picks up where the previous one left off, often by directly addressing a limitation flagged in the discussion.

- **Eye-tracking in reading (Portfolios 1-3).** Using the OneStop Eye Movements Dataset (Berzak et al., 2025; 360 participants reading news articles), I move from exploratory visualization of word-length and frequency effects on fixation behaviour (P1), to linear mixed-effects models of the GPT-2 surprisal × word-frequency interaction on dwell time (P2), and then decompose that interaction across first-pass and re-reading measures to isolate the processing stage at which it operates (P3).

- **Secondary analyses of an attention-capture experiment (Portfolios 4-8).** Building on Zhang & Gaspelin (2026, Experiment 3), I run three secondary analyses the original paper did not report - response time, saccade reaction time, and target fixation rate (P4-P6), followed by a full first-fixation probability decomposition that tracks where freed attention goes once the singleton is suppressed (P7), and a within-trial sequence analysis of post-capture recovery and search efficiency (P8).

- **Hidden Markov modelling of suppression learning (Portfolios 9-11).** A three-stage build of a 2-state joint HMM (item type + fixation duration) fit to Visual Search Task data: a proof-of-concept that recovers an Efficient-Search vs. Distractor-Engagement state structure (P9), participant-level feature extraction in the VST-first group (P10), and a regression testing whether those latent learning features predict cross-task transfer to an RSVP attentional blink for the consistent-distractor colour (P11).

The skills progress alongside the science — from `ggplot2` and base R, to `lme4`/`lmerTest` mixed-effects models, to fitting and decoding HMMs with `depmixS4`. The full source for every page lives in the [GitHub repository](https://github.com/mumizz/DS4P_Portfolio).
